A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison after matching renamed prompts and reordered appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation, grammaticality-judgment, gloss-prediction, vocabulary-coverage, and qualitative results, including supplementary experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds English–Guarani translation experiments.

M1.justification: Grammar-book partitioning, rule-based typological prompting, fine-tuning, and inference procedures are retained. Renaming P to PARA and expanding BOOK subset labels does not change the method; the additional extraction explanation does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Sections 3–4 add bidirectional English–Guarani translation using a Guarani grammar, Grambank features, and FLORES data. This introduces a third language with a substantial evaluation alongside Kalamang and Nepali. Grammaticality and glossing coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The existing translation comparators and five supervised glossing baselines remain in their corresponding experiments. Guarani extends the existing prompt comparisons to another language; newly cited research is not introduced as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Retained experiments preserve their splits, metrics, model versions, training settings, and first-line response extraction. Guarani follows the existing FLORES dev/devtest protocol with 1,012 test examples and the same context-length restrictions, rather than introducing a different evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Table 3 extends the full-book, parallel-only, explanation-only, and typological-prompt ablations to Guarani. Existing grammaticality tests, high-resource test-set checks, and seven qualitative translation cases are retained; their appendix relocation is not new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Figure 2's intervals as 95% confidence intervals and names the F-tests and Pearson correlations. v1 already reported confidence intervals and regression/correlation significance, so this refines statistical reporting without establishing additional runs or new testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds a substantial Guarani result block; Gemini scores 25.8 with BOOKpara versus 22.2 with BOOKall into Guarani. Existing translation and linguistic-task scores remain unchanged. Appendix coverage values also change: 5*-SHOT coverage moves from 58.3%/76.2% to 46.3%/67.8%, and TYP+BOOKpara coverage is revised. Associated regression R-squared values change from 0.87/0.86 to 0.84/0.87, retaining the significance conclusions.

T1.justification: No formal theory, proofs, mathematical definitions, or derivations are added or substantively revised. Changes to fitted regression equations and statistics concern empirical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly extend the finding about grammar explanations from Kalamang and Nepali to Guarani. The central claims about parallel data, competitive small-model fine-tuning, and typological prompting for linguistic tasks retain their meaning.

C2.justification: The discussion newly suggests that parallel prompts may work better because they resemble instruction-tuning data. Section 5 also qualifies Guarani-to-English Llama-I results by noting failures to place translations on the first line. Existing test-size and model-access limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises code, data, and grammar splits after review; v2 supplies a repository link and reports their availability in Section 4.1. It also specifies extraction based on text formatting. These improve access information and implementation documentation without demonstrating changed training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Estigarribia (2020), McMillan-Major (2020), Oncevay et al. (2020), and Ramos et al. (2024). It explicitly distinguishes textual typological prompts from continuous typological embeddings and clarifies glossing's relationship to earlier work. The central positioning against MTOB remains.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the abstract, introduction, related work, and methods. Prompt terminology is expanded, the Results subsection heading is removed, appendices are reordered, and acknowledgements and the publication header are added. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 expand for Guarani. Figure 1 is resized with its legend repositioned; Figure 2 is replotted with revised annotations and explicit 95% interval labels. Other changes concern table labels, captions, and appendix placement rather than a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The Guarani comparisons broaden the evidence for the central conclusion, while clearer terminology, explicit statistical reporting, and code/data access information improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. These gains are incremental: the small Kalamang test set remains, and output-format failures qualify some added Llama-I results. The revision strengthens the existing study without resolving its main limitations.
